satellite_subtitle: Remote control of model orientation using VR
satellite_technologies: Rpi.GPIO, pigpio, aiortc, WebRTC protocol, WebXR, Rasberry Pi 3B+
satellite_feature_1: control of the rotational position of the model without using an external arm
satellite_feature_2: receiving and transmitting images with minimal delay
satellite_feature_3: generation of an immersive image for playback in VR goggles based on data from a stereo camera
satellite_feature_4: a range of tools for testing the behavior of created systems
satellite_description_p1: The model was designed to check whether it is worthwhile to use VR to control the rotation of a satellite. To simplify the task, the rotation is performed in only one axis, but it still follows the same principles by which a satellite would rotate in space.
satellite_description_p2: For this purpose, it was necessary to create a physical model, test more than one method of controlling the rotary motor, and create a paper thoroughly analyzing such an application of virtual reality.
satellite_description_p3: Work on this topic as a whole became the subject of my master's thesis.
satellite_gallery_1_alt: Short video presenting the model and its functionality. The image shows a person wearing VR goggles and the model on a dedicated stand in the background.
satellite_gallery_2_alt: Photo of the model from two sides. The structure is made using 3D printing technology with white material. The lack of a housing allows the electronic components inside to be seen.
satellite_gallery_3_alt: Dedicated stand consisting of wooden supports and a metal rod on which the model is suspended.
snake_subtitle: A variant of the Snake game with local network multiplayer functionality
snake_description_p1: A spontaneous project that started as a quick, personal version of the Snake game and was then developed according to the motto "what else can I improve here."
snake_description_p2: It was an ideal place to experiment with object-oriented design paradigms, project structure, asynchronicity, and all networking-related issues such as: bandwidth, latency, message blocking on both the client and host side, as well as on intermediate devices invisible from the user's perspective.
snake_feature_1: asynchronous handling of the main game loop and interactive menu
snake_feature_2: object-oriented approach to controlling game elements
snake_feature_3: configurable game settings, including control buttons
snake_gallery_1_alt: Main menu of the Snake game. On a black background, a large 'SNAKE' title is shown, with the menu buttons below it. The 'PLAY' button is surrounded by a white outline.
snake_gallery_2_alt: Game screen. On a black background, a white snake made of touching circles forms a single curve. Colored single circles are placed in random locations. At the top of the screen, the current score and game time are shown.
snake_gallery_3_alt: Control button menu. On a black background, a large 'CONTROLS' title is shown, followed by a list of control buttons for 3 players. Each list item displays the selected control key.
snake_gallery_4_alt: Online lobby screen. On a black background, a large 'Network Room' title is shown, followed by the host's IP address and a list of connected players with their names, IP addresses, and ports.
cprofile_subtitle: Extension for VSCode facilitating the use of the CProfile module
cprofile_feature_1: using cprofile via the VSCode interface
cprofile_feature_2: line coloring and displaying execution time for each function in the working folder
cprofile_description_p1: An extension for VS Code that came in handy during another project. I couldn't find a free profiler that would conveniently show me where the bottlenecks in my application were, so I created my own.
cprofile_description_p2: However, there was no need to build the entire mechanism. After thoroughly checking available solutions, I found a program built into the Python language from which I could retrieve the necessary data. So I only wrote the extension that transforms this data into a convenient interface. This way, I gained the stability of a proven profiler and the convenience associated with a modern appearance.
cprofile_gallery_1_alt: Code of the program in Python. Lines with function names have red backgrounds in varying shades. The function names are followed by execution times expressed in seconds.
krita_subtitle: Plugin for the Krita graphics program that streamlines saving images
krita_feature_1: automation of saving a document and opening a new one with a single button (or keyboard shortcut)
krita_feature_2: support for predefining the dimensions of a new document
krita_feature_3: PyQt interface for creating new document groups, called sketchbooks
krita_description_p1: An extension for the Krita graphics editor, which I use regularly. Despite many useful existing features, it lacked the ability to create and save quick sketches without distractions in the form of the multi-step built-in export function.
krita_description_p2: The extension is meant to mimic the experience of using a real sketchbook, where the artist doesn't need to worry about what to name their work or where to put it, yet all their images remain organized according to the order they were created and bound together in a coherent form.
krita_description_p3: Such a solution significantly improves UX by drawing on the experiences of the average user, taken from real life.
krita_gallery_1_alt: Screenshot of the drop-down menu with the 'Sketchbook' option selected and expanded to show 4 plugin options such as: next page, export as page, open new.
krita_gallery_2_alt: Window titled 'Open new sketchbook'. Below title are fields for entering the sketchbook path, template, and prefix. At the bottom are the 'create' and 'cancel' buttons.
krita_gallery_3_alt: View of the Krita document with the image-saving window open. On the left, red text instructions explain how to quickly open a new sketchbook page.
krita_gallery_4_alt: View of a folder in the file explorer. All files start with the same prefix. PNG files end with a number. KRA files end with the words 'last' or 'template'.
